title: Aurora - Incident Postmortem Follow-up
summary: Follow-up on the April 18th production incident impacting inference latency and tail errors. Reviewed RCA, short-term mitigations, and roadmap items for reliability improvements and validation plan for Dedicated pools.
topics: Root cause (KV cache eviction + autoscaler config)
Security/audit log requests and KMS integration
Next steps: benchmarks, canary plans, docs
next_steps: Redwood to share final RCA doc and timeline by 2026-04-27
Customer to provide additional GPU host logs by 2026-04-26
Schedule load-run with Aurora traffic profile w/c 2026-05-04
Agree on canary rollout plan for Dedicated pool change by 2026-05-01
action_items: Samantha Lee: Share RCA doc and consolidated timeline by 2026-04-27
Raj Patel: Push autoscaler config hotfix to staging and run smoke tests by 2026-04-26
Miguel Santos: Send GPU host syslogs and prometheus scrape configs by 2026-04-26
Lina Park: Confirm compliance artifacts needed for audit log export by 2026-05-01
transcript:
[00:00] Samantha Lee: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We'll do a quick follow-up on the April 18th outage, review RCA and next steps. Was about 45 minutes total planned.
[00:12] Karen Thompson: Thanks, Samantha. Appreciate the recap — we had a second P1 yesterday with an unrelated service but this is the one from the 18th we need closure on.
[00:22] Raj Patel: Quick context, from Redwood side we traced the spike to a combination of aggressive autoscaler thresholds plus an unexpected KV cache eviction pattern during large fan-out requests. The eviction caused cold KV misses and a cascade of longer token generation times.
[00:40] Miguel Santos: When you say KV cache eviction, do you mean the prefix caching? We saw lots of cache miss rates go to 90% for a short window. The logs showed the liveness probe restarted a few pods as well.
[00:55] Raj Patel: Yeah, exactly. The runtime's prefix/K-V cache got thrashy when request concurrency spiked, and the autoscaler backoff was slow, so we temporarily had fewer warmed instances. There's also a config mismatch in your Dedicated pool: the burst policy was off and fallback routing wasn't prioritized to the smaller, lower-latency variant.
[01:15] Karen Thompson: Right, we had toggled burst to conserve credits — maybe that was the wrong call, but we need to understand mitigations.
[01:22] Samantha Lee: Totally. Short-term we patched the autoscaler threshold to bring up instances earlier and adjusted the cache retention thresholds. Raj, can you give the timeline for the hotfix we pushed?
[01:30] Raj Patel: Hotfix was applied on 2026-04-19 03:40 UTC — we lowered scale-up threshold from 80% to 60% cpu plus a custom token-queue metric. We also tweaked the K-V cache eviction limits to hold prefetched prefixes longer for those routes. Initial smoke tests looked good.
[01:48] Miguel Santos: I noticed lower tail latency in the next 6 hours but we still saw one 5xx around 04:15 UTC. Any idea?
[02:00] Raj Patel: That 5xx was from a secondary failure — a node OOM on a GPU host due to a mis-labeled model shard; suspect the orchestrator placed a heavy shard on a host with slightly different CUDA driver version. We're adding a preflight check for driver compatibility.
[02:18] Lina Park: From security perspective, we need the audit logs for the exact period and any change events tied to the Dedicated pool. Also, we'll want confirmation of KMS usage and whether any customer data was persisted outside of ephemeral caches.
[02:31] Samantha Lee: Understood. We will export the audit logs and send a pointer to the S3 archive (link: https://redwood.docs/aurora/audit-export-2026-04-18). For KMS, current Dedicated flow uses customer-managed keys via the KMS config you have, we didn't persist request payloads beyond ephemeral runtime caches.
[02:50] Miguel Santos: The link seems to have incomplete timestamps for a set of entries — some of the host-level logs are missing. I'll attach our prometheus scrape config and the host syslogs after the call.
[03:02] Raj Patel: Good. We'll also correlate the agent logs with the runtime metrics. One note — in a few transcriptions the product name appears as "Redwood Dedicated" or sometimes the engine name got garbled as "red wood run-time" in the automated export, ignore that, it's the same runtime.
[03:20] Karen Thompson: On long-term changes, what are we recommending? Increasing pool size, more aggressive pre-warming, changes to fallback model variants?
[03:29] Raj Patel: Recommended roadmap: 1) Default autoscaler improvements with token-queue metrics, 2) Stronger cache retention and warming heuristics for high-fanout routes, 3) Canary rollout of model-variant fallback with circuit breaker to limit error amplification, 4) Host compatibility preflight and stricter node labeling rules.
[03:48] Samantha Lee: We're proposing a staged approach — immediate hotfix (done), medium term (2-4 weeks) for warming heuristics and canary rollout, and longer term (quarterly) for autoscaler rewrite and improved observability.
[04:02] Miguel Santos: What do you need from Aurora to run the canary?
[04:07] Raj Patel: We'll need a traffic profile, typical concurrency percentiles, and a representative prompt set. Ideally a replay of 30 minutes of peak traffic to our staging environment. If we can get that w/c 2026-05-04 we can run the full load-run.
[04:22] Karen Thompson: We can generate a replay, but it contains PII in some prompts — is there a recommended scrub routine?
[04:28] Samantha Lee: Yes, we have a prompt-scrub template — we'll share the doc (link: https://redwood.docs/scrub-template). We can also accept hashed or redacted content; we do support private deployments if you need on-prem replay.
[04:42] Lina Park: For compliance, we also want to make sure audit log retention meets our SOC2 requirements — how long do you retain?
[04:49] Samantha Lee: Standard retention is 90 days in the hosted console, but for Dedicated we can extend retention or export to your S3. We'll outline options in the RCA.
[04:58] Miguel Santos: One ask — can we get an explicit list of what was changed in the cluster between 04/17 and 04/19? The change events show a config tweak but not the autoscaler thresholds.
[05:10] Raj Patel: We'll produce an event timeline with diffs. That will show the autoscaler threshold change at 03:40 UTC on 04/19 and the cache retention tweak at 03:45. We'll include the exact YAML diff.
[05:23] Karen Thompson: Great. Any risk of recurrence if we implement changes?
[05:28] Raj Patel: Risk goes down significantly but we advise observability additions: new SLOs on cache miss rates, token queue length, and an alert that triggers before scale-in happens if queue length > threshold. Also implement a soft-limit circuit breaker for model variants so failures don't cascade.
[05:44] Samantha Lee: We'll schedule a joint run to validate. Next action items are in the doc. Anything else from Aurora?
[05:51] Miguel Santos: Quick question on cost — if we increase pre-warmed capacity what's typical uplift?
[05:55] Samantha Lee: Roughly 8-15% depending on concurrency profile. Raj, do you have a ballpark?
[06:01] Raj Patel: Yeah, for your current traffic it should be closer to 10% unit cost increase but with a big drop in tail latency and 5xxs. We can run a cost/latency tradeoff chart and share.
[06:12] Karen Thompson: Ok that helps. Also please include the security summary for our auditors.
[06:18] Samantha Lee: Will do. We'll include KMS details, audit log exports, and the driver compatibility preflight steps.
[06:25] Miguel Santos: I'll upload the prometheus configs after the call and open a ticket with host syslogs.
[06:30] Samantha Lee: Thanks. Quick recap: Redwood to share RCA and timeline by 2026-04-27, Raj to push staging hotfix and tests by 2026-04-26, Aurora to provide logs and traffic profile by 2026-04-26, schedule load-run w/c 2026-05-04. We'll also set a follow-up to review canary results.
[06:50] Karen Thompson: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:55] Samantha Lee: Thanks all, we'll follow up via the Jira ticket and email with links.
[07:00] (call ends)
